annotation.title_clean: Socially interactive industrial robots: a PAD model of flow for emotional co-regulation
annotation.title_en: Socially interactive industrial robots: a PAD model of flow for emotional co-regulation
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Nunnari, F.; Tsovaltzi, D.; Lavit Nicora, M.; Beyrodt, S.; Prajod, P.; Chehayeb, L.; et al.
annotation.summary_en: Peer-reviewed article from the EU MindBot project. It presents a "covatar", a cobot paired with a virtual avatar, and the explainable BASSF emotional model, which uses PAD signals from facial analysis to co-regulate workers' emotions on assembly lines. Two empirical studies support using socially interactive industrial robots to improve worker wellbeing and flow. The paper does not address governance directly.
key_provisions_or_claims: The BASSF model (Boredom, Anxiety, Self-efficacy, Self-compassion, Flow) gives a transparent, theory-based way to drive interventions by the cobot and its avatar
The Dominance dimension of PAD predicts workers' self-efficacy and flow
Noisy PAD signals from facial analysis need pre-filtering and calibration for each user
Socially interactive industrial robots may improve worker wellbeing, job satisfaction and involvement
The paper argues for moving factories toward value-driven, worker-centred 'Industry 5.0' settings
